title: Integrating and Characterizing HPC Task Runtime Systems for hybrid AI-HPC workloads
problem: Hybrid AI-HPC workflows bottlenecked by Slurm srun throughput; srun unsuitable for dynamic heterogeneous tasks
motivation: Scientific workflows mix MPI/training/inference; throughput limited to 152 tasks/s; need better runtime systems
method: The researchers integrated RADICAL-Pilot, Flux, and Dragon runtime systems to manage compute resources through layered decision-making rather than a single scheduling point like Slurm's srun. In this approach, upper layers allocate resources across machines while lower layers handle task scheduling to individual processors, enabling rapid scheduling of diverse AI and HPC workloads. By distributing scheduling decisions across multiple components instead of routing everything through one bottleneck, they overcame Slurm's throughput limitation.
key_novelty: Combining RADICAL-Pilot, Flux, and Dragon runtime systems solves Slurm's throughput bottleneck, achieving over 1,500 task launches per second and reducing hybrid AI-HPC workflow completion time by 30–60%.
contributions: RADICAL-Pilot integration with Flux and Dragon
